---
title: "BII land use allocation"
bibliography: references.bib
---

## Summary

The NLC 2022 data were reclassified into broad land-use classes required by the BII workflow [@clements2026]. A second band records the available low, medium or high intensity class associated with the original land-cover category.

## Input data

-   South African National Land Cover 2022.
-   A BII reclassification table linking each source class to:
    1.  a broad BII land use class; and
    2.  selected intensity class.

The NLC thus is used for 2 classification frameworks: 1. broad land use classes and 2. Intensity classes. Protected areas are not assigned directly from national land cover. They are added later during segment allocation using the SAPAD layer.

## Data preparation

The original national land cover classes were grouped into six broad BII land-use categories:

| Value | BII land use       |
|------:|--------------------|
|     1 | Settlements        |
|     2 | Timber plantations |
|     3 | Tree crops         |
|     4 | Croplands          |
|     5 | Protected          |
|     6 | Untransformed      |

The preliminary intensity classes that could be used from the NLC 2022 were retained in a second band as:

| Value | Intensity class          |
|------:|--------------------------|
|     0 | No within class gradient |
|     1 | Unknown                  |
|     2 | Low                      |
|     3 | Medium                   |
|     4 | High                     |

## Analysis

Each NLC class was assigned a broad BII land-use value. Where the source classification distinguished intensity, it was also assigned a low, medium or high intensity class.

The resulting raster dataset contains three bands:

``` text
bii_land_use
bii_intensity_class
sanlc_class
```

The original national land-cover value is retained in `sanlc_class` for traceability.

## Output

Google Earth Engine asset:

``` text
NLC_reclass_BII_land_use_intensity
```
